pages.title: Custom Pass material nodes
pages.description: UE.DreamPassOutput writes the data a mesh pass draws, UE.DreamPassBuffer lets an ordinary material read an exported buffer; and how a pass material reads the pass's buffers with UE.UserSceneTexture. Needs UE 5.8.

pages.title: Math Builtins
pages.description: Unprefixed, HLSL-spelled call names — 44 HLSL names lowered straight to arithmetic material nodes, plus the four GLSL spellings a 1.x source may still use.

pages.title: Substrate Nodes
pages.description: The Substrate.* call namespace — every Substrate BSDF, composition and utility node of the running engine, called by name. UE 5.4+.

pages.title: UE.Expression
pages.description: The reflected call that creates any UMaterialExpression class of the builtin catalog by name — class resolution, argument dispatch, OutputType, output selection, Custom nodes and the result type.

pages.title: UE.* Nodes
pages.description: The 27 UE.* names 1.x implemented itself and their argument lists, the bases of the two transform builtins, the three special-cased names, and the Properties declaration form.

pages.title: DreamShader Plugin
pages.description: Release notes for the DreamShader Unreal plugin, newest first, taken from the plugin's own CHANGELOG.

pages.title: HLSL passes
pages.description: The HLSL a compute pass, or a fullscreen pass without a material, runs — written in an hlsl block of the .dsp or in a .usf, the names its bindings make, the fixed parameters and helpers of DreamPass.ush, and how the code reaches the engine through a pre-check and a snapshot. Needs UE 5.8.

pages.title: Custom Pass runtime
pages.description: What happens to a compiled .dsp pipeline at run time — what makes it apply to a view, when its passes run, what its buffers hold, how exported buffers reach materials, Blueprints, UMG and Niagara, and how to see what it did. Needs UE 5.8.

pages.title: Diagnostics
pages.description: Where DreamShader's diagnostics appear, how to read one, how the DSHnnnn codes are banded, their severities, a table of the common ones by stage, and the 1.x messages mapped to their codes.

pages.title: Limitations
pages.description: What DreamShader 2.1.2 does not do — the language boundaries of a 1.x Graph and of .dss, what 1.x did that still happens but is now said out loud, the decompiler's gaps, the function-level ceiling on material layers, and the engine-version and Custom Pass boundaries.

pages.title: Custom Pass examples
pages.description: Seven complete .dsp pipelines with the .dss materials they use — highlight outline, UI frosted glass, X-ray, wind field, scanner pulse, old CRT, tagged objects. Needs UE 5.8.

pages.title: Patterns
pages.description: The file-shaped building blocks of DreamShaderLang — minimal material, parameters, texture sampling, shared headers, functions, UE.* nodes, layers, VirtualFunction, GraphFunction and Layout — each one a complete source file, with the .dss form beside the 1.x one.

pages.title: Recipes
pages.description: Complete DreamShaderLang materials — animated tint, panning UVs, branching, static-switch variants, translucent UI, PBR, MaterialAttributes, Substrate, parameter collections, a multi-output helper, a Settings tour and Runtime Virtual Texture, each as a .dsm and as a .dss.

pages.title: Asset Paths

pages.description: Loops, return, ternary, %, comparisons and indexing — every HLSL / GLSL construct a Graph block does not implement, the code the compiler reports for it, and what to write instead.

pages.title: Substrate sugar
pages.description: Operators and lerp over Substrate values, legacy parameters on a slab, run-time branches, values built member by member, and one source for Substrate and non-Substrate projects.

pages.title: Metadata and Groups

pages.title: Asset References

pages.title: Property Types

pages.title: Backend

pages.title: Enum Values

pages.title: Material Settings

pages.title: Project Settings
pages.description: All 17 properties under Project Settings ▸ DreamPlugin ▸ Dream Shader, their real config identifiers, defaults and effects, and the Custom Pass settings object.

pages.description: What the plugin is, the five modules it ships, which engines it supports, and where the related repositories live.
